result.rationale: The diff adds `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and passes it directly to `members.offset(offset)` in groups_controller#members with no clamping. Unlike the JS client (which uses Math.max(...,0)), the server accepts arbitrary params, and a negative value into ActiveRecord's offset would raise a StatementInvalid on PostgreSQL, producing a 500 rather than a 4xx.

judged_text: The members endpoint passes params[:offset].to_i straight into the SQL offset clause without clamping, so offset=-1 produces a negative OFFSET that PostgreSQL rejects. A request to /groups/:name/members.json?offset=-1 raises ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx, breaking any caller that paginates backwards past zero.

A request to /groups/:name/members.json?offset=-1 raises ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx, breaking any caller that paginates backwards past zero.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then unconditionally calls `.offset(offset)` (see `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`). There is no clamping to `>= 0`, so a request like `?offset=-1` will pass a negative offset into ActiveRecord/PostgreSQL, which can raise an error and produce a 500. This diff also expands pagination to all groups (not just automatic), increasing exposure to the issue.
